content.thinking: I need to fix repeated "three times" phrasing throughout — things like "on any of the three reads," "three investigation rounds," and "Argus repeated the same investigation three times" should be varied. I should also drop "a minute or so" since it references a specific time duration, while "within seconds" is fine to keep.

action_items.item: Add a regression test for the zero-spend case in the spend summary code, and make the summary handle a zero divisor explicitly. This is separate from reviewing the proposed fix.
Make every change to monthly-spend-feature and other flags, including percentage ramps and targeting changes, appear in the flag provider history and the production change events that Argus reads.

Let the Mitigation Agent propose disabling a flag when logs show errors only on the flag-on code path and the error rate rose as evaluations shifted to on, even if no change event is recorded. A human approves the action.
Roll flags out progressively, with an automatic halt and rollback when the error rate of the affected service rises above baseline.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers saw account page requests fail. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average and peaked at {errors_at_worst}, starting at {began}. The service had not recovered at the last metrics read.
The failing requests raised ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code (spend_summary.py). These errors first appear in the same minute the error rate rose.
That code path runs only when monthly-spend-feature evaluates as on. Evaluations were all off before {began}. In the onset minute they were mostly on, and they were all on afterwards.
The code behind the flag does not guard against a zero divisor, so once the flag exposed it to real traffic it failed on every request that hit the zero case.

The record cannot say why the flag turned on. The flag provider showed no recent flag changes in any investigation round, and no production deploys or releases were found. The candidates' claim of a toggle is inferred from the evaluation logs and was not confirmed by a change event.

contributing_factors.factor: The spend summary code has no guard or test for the zero-divisor case, so enabling it for live traffic produced a crash.

Flag state changes, including gradual ramps, did not appear in the flag provider's history or the change events. The flag moved from off to on with no recorded change, and the investigation could not tie the failures to a change.

Argus could not propose a mitigation such as turning the flag off. Its mitigation step found no recent flag change and refused to act. It repeated the investigation and then moved to a code fix, so the failing path stayed live while the fix was drafted.
The flag's rollout was not gated on service health, so a failing code path reached nearly all traffic almost at once with no automatic halt.

input.executive_summary: From {began}, a large share of shopper requests to the account pages in io-shop failed. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to an average of {errors_while_broken} and peaked at {errors_at_worst}. The service had not recovered by the last metrics read, so it was broken for at least {duration}, and that figure is a lower bound. The failures came from a newly active spend-summary feature that crashes on a division by zero. Argus's investigator reached the same cause in every round. No mitigation was proposed, so nothing was changed in production. Argus opened a draft pull request with a code fix and escalated to humans after {held}. The fix still needs review and merge.

went_well: The Investigator placed the onset at {began} and found the ZeroDivisionError within seconds of starting, and every round reached the same flag-related explanation.
The Code-Fix Agent produced a draft pull request and Argus escalated to a human after {held}.
went_wrong: No mitigation was ever proposed. Argus repeated the same investigation several times with the same evidence, took no action, and the service had not recovered when the incident was handed over.
The candidates stated that the flag was toggled, but the flag provider history showed no change. The explanation was never tested because no action was tried.

input.root_cause: The code path behind the monthly-spend-feature flag divides by zero in spend_summary.py. The flag began evaluating as on for nearly all traffic at {began}, so account page requests that reached that path raised ZeroDivisionError. The flag provider and the deploy history recorded no change, so nothing explains why the flag turned on.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
